body:
The heavy-suite lock is two locks. A tree at or past #1264 takes a flock on
`/tmp/codeaf-suite-<uid>.lockfile`. A tree behind #1264 takes the older
directory lock at `/tmp/codeaf-suite-<uid>.lock`. Neither mechanism can see the
other, so the flock's exclusivity is at present a CLAIM THE BOX DOES NOT HONOUR.

## Observed on the box, 2026-09-20T18:35:25Z

A heavy suite running while the flock reads free:

- pid 4029204, `bash ./scripts/one-suite.sh go test -timeout 15m -count=1
  -count=1 -p 1 ./cmd/codeaf ./internal/tui3`, cwd
  `/home/santosh/src/cw0918-adaptive-folders`, alive.
- pid 4029208, its `go test`, alive.
- That tree is at `991a83d384f5197e99471bb05b4ac8a4d3c1b07e`, behind #1264. Its
  `scripts/one-suite.sh:31` reads `lock="/tmp/codeaf-suite-$(id -u).lock"`, with
  the comment explaining that the lock is a directory because mkdir is atomic.
- `/tmp/codeaf-suite-1001.lock` exists, created 14:29, and its `pid` file
  contains `4029204`, the live process.
- At the same instant `flock -n /tmp/codeaf-suite-1001.lockfile -c true` returns
  0, free, `lsof` on that file returns no holder, and the file's contents are a
  stale line from an earlier run at 18:12:10Z.

That run is behaving CORRECTLY by its own rules. It holds a lock. It is simply
holding one that current readers do not read.

## The failure is symmetric, and only one direction has been hit

DIRECTION ONE, live tonight. A stale tree holds the directory lock. A current
reader checks only the flock, sees free, and starts a second heavy suite beside
it. This is the direction that has been costing us unattributable reds and
timing numbers taken under contention nobody recorded.

DIRECTION TWO, not yet hit and worse. A current tree holds the flock. A stale
tree's runner checks only the directory, sees no holder, and starts beside it.
Same collision, opposite parties, and here the party clobbered is the one that
did everything right.

Dual-checking on the READ side fixes direction one only. It stops a current
reader starting beside a stale holder. It does nothing to stop a stale runner
starting beside a current holder, because that runner will never be taught to
read the flock: being unaware of the flock is what makes it stale.

## Immediate remedy, for anything that reads the lock

Wait on the directory lock first and the flock second. Both, in that order. A
gate doing this today can see pid 4029204 and queues behind it correctly.

## Durable remedy, for the shared script, and the reason to prefer it

During the transition, the current `scripts/one-suite.sh` should take BOTH
locks: the flock as now, and the old directory lock as well. It costs a mkdir.

What it buys is that a current tree becomes VISIBLE TO EVERY STALE READER STILL
OUT THERE, without any stale tree being changed. The invisibility then runs in
one direction only, and that direction is the safe one: a stale runner sees a
current holder and waits. Direction two closes without touching anything that is
behind the head.

The transition ends when nothing running on the box is behind #1264. Until
somebody can assert that, dual-hold is what makes the flock's claim true rather
than merely declared.

## Consequences worth recording while this is open

- Any `suite_lock_held` field written by a flock-only reader is false on exactly
  the runs where it matters.
- A ceiling that lowers while a suite holds the lock has not been lowering for
  these runs.
- Timing numbers taken "under the lock" during the transition are upper bounds
  with an unknown floor, and should be quoted that way rather than discarded.

Raised as an issue and not a patch because it changes a shared script that other
trees run.
